en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Those Who Have Been Maidens.
83. The Training Rule on One Year:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were ordaining two [novices] in one year.
Consequently, the residence was not sufficient,
and people likewise complained, grumbled, and became indignant:
“How can these bhikkhunīs ordain two [nuns] in a single year?
The residence will not be sufficient for them.
The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, grumbling, and criticizing in this way.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires... they complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"How indeed can these bhikkhunīs ordain two [novices] in one year? ...
"Is it true, monks, that these bhikkhunīs ordain two [novices] in one year?"
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How can it be, monks, that bhikkhunīs will give the full admission to two [nuns] in one year?”
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, should the nuns recite this training rule:
‘If any nun should give the full admission to two [nuns] in one year, it is an offense entailing confession.’”
"But whichever" means whichever such... "nun" means...
[as before]... nun.
...pe... this is the nun intended in this context.
"One year" means one full year.
“Two [nuns] shall ordain”: she shall grant full admission to two.
If, thinking “I will ordain two,” she seeks a group, a preceptor, a bowl, or a robe, or she demarcates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For the motion, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For the two formal proclamations, there are offenses of wrong-doing.
At the conclusion of the formal proclamation, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya) for the preceptor.
There is an offense of wrong-doing for the group and for the preceptor.
There is no offense if she ordains one person at a time.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of one who is a first-offender.
The thirteenth training rule is concluded.
The eighth chapter: The Chapter on Those Who Have Been Maidens.
